translationRepairs: The corner bracket belongs to the Chinese annotation markup and should not remain in English.
The literal field contains the same stray annotation bracket.
When the Prince of Yan's army entered the capital, he welcomed them and submitted; he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Revenue.
When the Prince of Yan's army entered the capital, he welcomed them and submitted; he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
The preceding sentence makes Jian Yi Right Vice Minister of Personnel; 左侍郎 is his promotion within that ministry.
He then returned to manage affairs at the Ministry of Revenue.
He then returned to manage the affairs of the Ministry of Personnel.
部 refers to the Ministry of Personnel headed by Jian Yi, not Revenue.
The following year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister of Revenue.
The following year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister of Personnel.
Guo Jin replaced Jian Yi in the Ministry of Personnel; Revenue is not supported here.
In the seventh year of the reign an edict ordered the authorities to build Jian Yi a new residence inside the Wenhua Gate.
In the seventh year of the reign an edict ordered the authorities to build Jian Yi a new residence inside the Wenming Gate.
文明門 is Wenming Gate; Wenhua Gate would be written 文華門.
In the seventh year an edict ordered the authorities to build Yi a new residence inside the Wenhua Gate.
In the seventh year an edict ordered the authorities to build Yi a new residence inside the Wenming Gate.
The paired literal field requires the same correction from Wenhua to Wenming Gate.
He was soon given Vice Minister Li Wenyu as deputy, and Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again dispatched with an imperial book on water control as a gift.
He was soon given Vice Minister Li Wenyu as deputy, and Assistant Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again dispatched with an imperial book on water control as a gift.
僉都御史 is Assistant Censor-in-Chief, subordinate to 都御史, not Censor-in-Chief.
He was transferred to assistant minister of justice and acted for the Ministry of Revenue.
He was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and acted for the Ministry of Revenue.
The corpus standard for 大理丞 is Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
He was transferred to Assistant Minister of Justice and acted for the Revenue Ministry.
He was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and acted for the Revenue Ministry.
The literal field should use the same institutional hierarchy for 大理丞.
Zou Shiyan was a native of Yidu.
The received text has 宣都, but the older Ming Waishi witness and the known county identify Zou as a native of 宜都; the proposal must preserve Yidu.
When the Yan army entered, he welcomed and submitted; he was transferred to Left Vice Minister.
When the Yan army entered, he welcomed and submitted; he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
The preceding office establishes that 左侍郎 is Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
Within a few months he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
Within a few months he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
Jian Yi remained in Personnel and was promoted from its Left Vice Minister to its Minister.
Several months later, he was advanced to Minister.
Several months later, he was advanced to Minister of Personnel.
The literal field should make the abbreviated ministry explicit from the immediate context.
He returned to handle the ministry's affairs.
He returned to handle the affairs of the Ministry of Personnel.
The literal field correctly resolves 部 as Jian Yi’s Ministry of Personnel.
The next year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister.
The next year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister of Personnel.
The literal field should identify the ministry in which Guo Jin replaced Jian Yi.
Soon Vice Minister Li Wenyu was ordered as his deputy, and Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again sent bearing a book on water control as a gift.
Soon Vice Minister Li Wenyu was appointed his deputy, and Assistant Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again sent bearing a book on water control as a gift.
This paired correction restores Assistant Censor-in-Chief and the appointment construction 命...為之副.
Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu served as his deputy.
Yuan Fu, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, served as his deputy.
大理少卿 is Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, not a vice minister of justice.
Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu served as his deputy.
Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Fu served as his deputy.
The literal field requires the same institutional correction for 大理少卿.

Yu Shiji, style Yongzhen, came from Xiangshan. During Jianwen he was training instructor at Yanzhou. After submitting a memorial on current policy, he was promoted to censor. Sent to inspect Fengyang, Huizhou, and Huguang, he distinguished and released wrongfully imprisoned men. When Chengzu took the throne, Yu was advanced to assistant censor-in-chief. By imperial order he carried books on water management to Yuanji, and he stayed on to supervise agricultural administration in western Zhejiang. Huzhou owed as much as six hundred thousand shi of grain, and his colleagues wanted to report a reduced figure. Shiji said, "To deceive the ruler and harm the people is something I will not do." He reported the facts in full, and all the arrears were remitted. Soon afterward he was impeached by Censor-in-chief Chen Ying and imprisoned together with Yuan Fu, vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review. Yuan Fu died in prison, and Shiji was demoted to managing official and assigned to water control in Suzhou and Songjiang. Later he was restored to office. On his return he submitted the Shengxiao ruiying song. The emperor said, "You are a great minister, yet instead of speaking of the people's benefits and harms, you offer flattery?" and threw it back to him. Early in Xuande, Shiji reached the post of vice minister in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and retired.

Yu Shiji, style Yongzhen, was from Xiangshan. During Jianwen he served as training instructor at Yanzhou. He submitted a letter discussing current policy and was promoted to censor. Sent out to inspect Fengyang, Huizhou, and Huguang, he was able to distinguish and release wrongful imprisonments. When Chengzu came to the throne, he was advanced to assistant censor-in-chief. Under imperial order, he took books on water management and bestowed them on Yuanji, and therefore remained to supervise agricultural administration in western Zhejiang. Huzhou owed as much as six hundred thousand shi of grain; his colleagues wanted to reduce the number in reporting it. Shiji said, "To deceive the ruler and harm the people is something I will not do." He fully memorialized the truth, and all were exempted. Soon he was impeached by Chen Ying, censor-in-chief, and was imprisoned together with Yuan Fu, vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review. Fu died in prison, and Shiji was demoted to managing official and put to work on water control in Suzhou and Songjiang. Later he was restored to office, and on returning submitted the Shengxiao ruiying song. The emperor said, "You are a great minister, yet instead of speaking of the people's benefits and harms, you present flattery?" He threw it back to him. At the beginning of Xuande, Shiji served up to vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and retired.
